claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout is monitored and reversible, provided the known procurement invoice review weakness is explicitly disclosed in the model card rather than treated as cured by rollout controls.
decision_criteria: Verdict would move toward compliant if admissible evidence shows the exposed procurement invoice review limitation is explicitly disclosed in the pre-launch model card or equivalent launch artifact.
Verdict would also move toward compliant if the affected segment is excluded from rollout before launch.
Verdict would also move toward compliant if there is a completed, reviewed, and approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed segment.
Absent one of those conditions, launch certification remains unsupported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Final model card or launch artifact showing explicit disclosure of the procurement invoice review limitation for the named launch use case.
Approval record showing the disclosure was reviewed and accepted as satisfying release policy before launch.
If disclosure is not the path, a completed and approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses procurement invoice review exposure.
specific_concerns: The affected procurement invoice review segment remains exposed in the initial cohort, so rollout controls do not neutralize the weakness under the stated policy.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance; the draft is unsigned and omits the exposed segment.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed or approved for the named launch use case.
The actor's packet is directionally aligned with policy only if disclosure is truly implemented; that predicate is not evidenced in the record.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable, rather than only conditionally supportable after verified disclosure is completed.
Any implication that monitored rollout, 6% launch, rollback capability, or lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents can substitute for the missing disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any inference that existing risk acceptance coverage addresses procurement invoice review exposure.
